## Why the classes are shaped like this

Each class carries seven things, and the last three are the ones that decide whether the class is
worth having:

| Field | What it forces |
| --- | --- |
| `definition` | A sentence a second reader would apply the same way |
| `detected_by` | `engine`, `human` or `both` — never implied |
| `engine_checks` | The real check names in the product, or nothing. A class mapped to a check that no longer runs is a lie with a citation in it, and `test_engine_check_ids_match_the_product_exactly` fails when that drifts |
| `fix_target` | Where the repair goes: `prompt`, `check`, `screen`, `policy`, `workflow`. A class whose fix target is "model" is not a class, it is a wish |
| `default_severity` | `block`, `advisory` or `label` — how the class reads, not whether the product blocks. Blocking is owned by `quality.py`; six classes carry `block` (E10, E11, E13, E14, E20, E24) |
| `observable` | The thing a person could point at. A class with no observable is decoration, and `test_every_class_names_an_observable_and_a_detector` refuses it |

The dataclass also declares `inter_reader`, and **it is empty on all 26 classes** (measured
2026-10-09: 0 of 26 filled). That is the honest state of an ambition, not a field: whether two
clinicians would apply the same label is the question that decides whether a class is usable, and
answering it here would be engineering guessing at clinical agreement. It stays empty until a
ratified case is labelled twice, and
[`PROTOCOL.md`](PROTOCOL.md) §5 lists it as something the first study must collect.

## Where each class maps to a metric

The brief asked that every error map to a definition, a detection method, a severity and a metric.
The first three are fields above. The fourth is deliberately **one metric for all classes**, not
twenty-six: a class's measure is its labelled count per 100 cases, published by
`reporting._aggregate()` as `error_classes` and `error_classes_by_group`, with `unclassified_rate`
beside it. What differs between classes is *who supplies the label* — `detected_by` — not how it is
counted. Twenty-six per-class metrics would be twenty-six denominators to negotiate, and §6 of
[`METRICS.md`](METRICS.md) is the record of what happens to metrics whose denominator is
negotiable.

## The four groups

- **content** (12) — what the report says. This is where clinical harm lives, and where engine
  coverage is highest: 8 of 12 have a detector.
- **form** (3) — how it is written and structured. `E13 format_breach` and `E14 truncated` block;
  `E15 style_or_readability` never does, because a style problem is not a safety event and treating
  it as one is how a reviewer stops reading the warnings.
- **process** (6) — what the work cost. `E20 degradation_unannounced` is the only process class that
  blocks, and [`../INVARIANTS.md`](../INVARIANTS.md) P13 explains why it is the platform's worst
  class: a lesser answer given where a promised one was required, with nothing saying so.
- **evidence** (5) — the system failing to measure itself. `E24 unmeasurable_claim` blocks: a number
  reported without its instrument, denominator, or the fact that the input was synthetic. This group
  exists because the alternative is that measurement failures are filed under "engineering".

## Engine coverage is low, and that is the finding

9 of 26 classes have an engine detector — 34.6% overall, 66.7% of the content classes — and 9 classes
are labelled `human` alone. That is not a backlog item:
[`../product/ROADMAP.md`](../product/ROADMAP.md) §4.1 measured a hypothetical tenth check that
catches 85% of hallucination probes by flagging 17 words on every correct report, and the narrower
version catches 11% while touching 41 of 100 correct answers — every one of those 41 legitimate. A
radiology report's *meaning* is not pattern-matchable, so the human is the check, and the taxonomy
says which classes the human is needed for instead of pretending otherwise.

Two readings of the table are easy to get wrong, so they are stated here:

- **`E02 invented_finding` has `fix_target: check` and no `engine_checks`.** That pair is deliberate
  and means *the check that would catch this does not exist, and building one blind was measured and
  refused*. A fix target names where a repair belongs, not where one works.
- **`E14` and `E20` say `detected_by: engine` with no check named.** They are machine-decidable from
  the platform's own fields — a finish reason, a `degraded` flag with no reader-visible statement —
  without belonging to the nine quality checks. `test_no_class_claims_a_detector_it_cannot_have`
  forbids the opposite confusion: a class naming a check while claiming only a human can decide it.
  Three classes used to do exactly that, and the published coverage figure counted a detector that
  fires on a different error.

## E99 exists so the register stays honest

`unclassified` is a class, and `reporting._aggregate()` publishes `unclassified_rate` as a metric in
its own right. If it rises, the taxonomy is wrong — that is the only way this document can be proved
incomplete by data rather than by argument. `E25 misclassified_label` is its counterpart: a label
applied to the wrong class, which is a defect of the measuring system, not of the draft.

## Versioning

`evidence.TAXONOMY_VERSION` is 1. It travels inside every session record, because a stored label
from version 1 is only comparable to another version-1 label. Adding, removing or redefining a class
bumps it, and the bump is a *minor* change only when nothing that was blocking becomes non-blocking;
otherwise it is a change to a threshold, and
[`../GOVERNANCE.md`](../GOVERNANCE.md) owns that decision.

## Adding a class

1. It must be observable, and name a fix target that exists.
2. It must not overlap a class already present — if it does, the right change is to the existing
   class's definition, and that is a version bump with a diff a clinician can read.
3. Its `engine_checks` entries must be real names in `futurekind_radiology.quality`, or empty.
4. `python -m evidence taxonomy --markdown` regenerates the table above; nothing here is hand-typed.
5. If the class changes what blocks a report, it is a clinical decision, not a taxonomy edit.

## Drift check

The check that fails when this file drifts is `test_codes_are_unique_and_namespaced` and
`test_every_class_names_an_observable_and_a_detector` in `scripts/validation/test_evidence.py`, plus
`python -m evidence taxonomy --markdown`, which regenerates the table above. The coverage figures in
§"Engine coverage" are the `engine_coverage` output of that same command, measured 2026-10-09.
